source.title: String .removeTags() deletes the rest of the text after a < that is not a tag

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body: ### Bug Description `String.removeTags()` deletes everything after a `<` that does not start a tag. `"price < 100 USD".removeTags()` returns `"price "` instead of `"price < 100 USD"`, and `"a<2 and b>1".removeTags()` returns `"a1"`. The function uses `value.replace(/<[^>]*>?/gm, '')`. Because the closing `>` is optional, any `<` matches up to the next `>` or, when there is none, to the end of the string. Plain-text content that contains a less-than sign (prices, comparisons, `<3`, `x <= y`) loses part of its text silently. An HTML parser only starts a tag when `<` is followed by a letter, `/`, `!` or `?`; a `<` followed by a space or digit is text. The same code is in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`. ### To Reproduce 1. Evaluate `{{ "price < 100 USD".removeTags() }}` in an expression. 2. You get `price ` (the text after `<` is gone). Minimal Node reproduction of the same regex: ```sh node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify("price < 100 USD".replace(/<[^>]*>?/gm, "")))' # "price " ``` ### Expected behavior `price < 100 USD`: only real tags are removed, as in `"bold, link".removeTags()` → `"bold, link"`. ### Debug Info Found by reading the code on `master`, and reproduced with a unit test that calls `stringExtensions.functions.removeTags` directly. ### Operating System Ubuntu Linux ### n8n Version master (current HEAD) ### Node.js Version 20.19.2 ### Database SQLite (default) ### Execution mode main (default)

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: Both current implementations use the same `/<[^>]*>?/gm` replacement: one in `packages/workflow`, one in `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime`. The workflow test currently covers nested tags, but not a less-than sign in plain text; I also could not find a `removeTags` case in the expression-runtime test file. Regression cases for `price < 100 USD` and `a<2 and b>1`, alongside the existing tag example, would pin down the behavior in both implementations.

comments.author: kevin9327
comments.text: Thanks for checking both copies. The PR already changes the regex in `packages/workflow` and `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime`, and the expression-runtime tests cover `price < 100 USD`, `a<2 and b>1` and `x <= y`. You're right that the workflow side only had the nested-tag case, so I pushed a commit adding `price < 100 USD`, `a<2 and b>1` and `bold < 100` to `packages/workflow/test/ExpressionExtensions/string-extensions.test.ts`. All three fail with the old `/<[^>]*>?/gm` pattern and pass with the new one.
